Goal

Reach root on a black-box Linux box whose weak points are leaked secrets and a Docker setup.

Setup

A Linux target VM on a bridged network with 4 GB RAM and 1 vCPU.

Black-box: only a low-privilege SSH login and the target address were given. All exploitation was manual, with no Metasploit.

Redacted on purpose: Token · Flags

What I did

Enumerated the system and read the bash history, which hinted at a service token.

Read a flag file that was world-readable (mode 644, CWE-732).

Listed processes with ps aux and recovered the token from the command-line arguments of a root-run sync script (CWE-214).

Used the same token as the password of a second user (CWE-255) and moved laterally.

Found a sudoers rule that allowed docker compose exec as root, entered the shipping container, and escaped through the mounted Docker socket by starting a new container that mounts the host filesystem.

Results

Root in 44:44, with all five flags captured.

Four findings: 2 critical (token leak through process arguments, exposed Docker socket) and 2 high (token reuse, misconfigured sudoers). The write-up rates the system critical.

A token in CLI arguments is visible to every local user through procfs (CWE-214), and access to the host Docker socket is equivalent to root.

Log signal: ps aux / process auditing shows --auth-token in argv; docker.sock volume mount

What failed

nsenter failed with Operation not permitted, because it needs CAP_SYS_PTRACE.

The first Docker escape failed: the host bind mount did not populate as expected in the new container, likely because of the order of the docker run arguments. The second attempt succeeded.

Next

Never pass secrets as command-line arguments; use a protected environment file or a secrets manager.

Do not mount the Docker socket into containers unless truly needed; consider Podman or rootless Docker.

Use separate credentials for the API and for SSH, and rotate them.

Restrict sudoers to least privilege and keep Docker access away from non-admin users.

Withheld on purpose: credentials , flags and lab IPs .
